name: cell-sorting
title: Differential-adhesion cell sorting
question:
Given two cell types with unequal contact energies, does the wrapped CompuCell3D
engine reorganise an initially mixed blob so that like cells associate — the
Steinberg differential-adhesion effect — driven entirely through the Process's
typed config?
hypothesis:
With type-A homotypic adhesion strong (low contact energy) and type-B weaker,
minimising interfacial energy drives the two populations to segregate while the
total cell count is conserved.
objective:
Initialise a mixed two-type blob on an 80x80 lattice, advance the real engine for
3000 Monte-Carlo steps through `CompuCell3DProcess`, and read cell counts and
morphometry back through the wrapper's output ports.
description:
A canonical Cellular-Potts sorting setup: two cell populations (type A, type B) start
mixed; differential contact energies make unlike-unlike interfaces costly, so the
system lowers its energy by clustering like cells and smoothing type boundaries. The
run is a single real cc3d 4.6.0 trajectory; nothing here is reimplemented.
claim:
The wrapper drives genuine differential-adhesion sorting: the 45-cell population
(16 type-A, 29 type-B) is conserved while the mean cell surface rises from 22.3 to
28.0 px over 3000 MCS as cells reorganise and like-cell boundaries consolidate.
expected_behavior: Total cell count is conserved (no growth/death terms).
Cells segregate by type; the animated scene shows like cells associating over time.
Mean cell surface changes as boundaries reorganise.

readouts.name: Cell population
readouts.description: Conserved at 45 (16 type-A, 29 type-B) throughout the run.

readouts.name: Spatial segregation
readouts.description: Segregation of the two cell types, shown in the committed animated scene.

behavior_tests.name: Differential adhesion drives sorting on the real engine
behavior_tests.description:
The two-type CPM composite runs on cc3d 4.6.0 through the single-Process wrapper,
conserves the population, and produces the expected sorting morphology (committed
animated scene + morphometry charts).

limitations: Sorting is shown qualitatively (animated scene) plus scalar morphometry; a quantitative segregation statistic (e.g. heterotypic boundary length) is a natural follow-up but is not computed here.
